Rashi on Pesachim 8a:10:1.hebrew: במסתפק - אוצר שמסתפק הימנו יין לשולחנו צריך בדיקה. פעמים שהשמש נכנס להביא יין כשהוא כלה על השולחן, ופתו בידו:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:10:1.english: Where one supplies - A storeroom from which one supplies wine for his table requires searching. At times, the attendant enters to bring wine when it runs out on the table, with his bread in his hand.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:11:1.hebrew: יש קבע לאכילה - יודע הוא כמה שמן צריך לכך וכך בני אדם, ומביאו קודם סעודה, ואין צריך לעמוד מן השלחן ולהביא. אבל יין, אין קבע לשתיה — פעמים ששתיית סעודה מרובה משל אתמול, ואין השמש בקי בדבר:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:11:1.english: There is a fixed [quantity] for eating - He knows how much oil is needed for such-and-such [number of] people, and brings it before the meal, and does not need to get up from the table and bring [more]. But [for] wine, there is no fixed [quantity] for drinking — at times the drinking of [a] meal is greater than that of yesterday, and the attendant is not expert in the matter.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:12:1.hebrew: עשו אוצרות שכר בבבל - להצריך בדיקה במסתפק, כאוצרות יין בארץ ישראל, דכיון דרגילין בו, אין קבע לשתייתו:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:12:1.english: [The Sages] rendered beer storages in Babylonia - To require a search [for leaven] in [a storage from which] one draws supplies, like wine storages in Eretz Yisrael; for since they are accustomed to it, there is no fixed [amount] for drinking it.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:13:1.hebrew: הא ברברבי - אין צריך בדיקה, שיש להם קבע ואומד, ואין צריך לעמוד ולהביא באמצע הסעודה:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:13:1.english: This [refers to] large [fish] - [It] does not require searching, for they have a fixed [quantity] and an estimate, and one does not need to get up and bring [more] in the middle of the meal.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:13:2.hebrew: זוטרי - אין להם קבע ואומד, וצריך לעמוד ולהביא:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:13:2.english: Small [fish] - They do not have a fixed [amount] and estimate, and one needs to get up and bring [more].

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:14:1.english: A salt storage - A storehouse for salt.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:14:2.hebrew: ובי קירי - שעוה. צריך בדיקה, לפי שעומד מתוך הסעודה להביא מלח ונרות:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:14:2.english: And a storage for candles - [Kirei means] wax. [They] require searching, because one gets up from the meal to bring salt and candles.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:15:1.hebrew: דנפל - אם נפל הבנין, אין מחייבין אותו לבדוק את גל אבנים אלא למראית העין, אבל לא להכניס ידו ביניהן. ומתחלה, כשהיה הכותל קיים, נשתמש בחוריו, ועכשיו נפל, ויש שם סכנת עקרבים, שדרכן לימצא באשפות ובגלין:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:15:1.english: Where it fell - If the building collapsed, we do not obligate him to search the heap of stones except for what is visible to the eye, but not to insert his hand between them. And initially, when the wall was standing, he made use of its holes, and now it has collapsed, and there is a danger of scorpions there, as it is their nature to be found in refuse heaps and mounds [of stones].

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:16:1.hebrew: בשאין הכלב יכול לחפש אחריו - הכי מפרש לה ר"ש בפ"ב. ותניא: כמה חפישת הכלב? שלשה טפחים:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:16:1.english: Where a dog cannot search for it - This is how Rabban Shimon [ben Gamliel] explains it in the second chapter. And it was taught [in a baraita]: How much is a dog's search? Three handbreadths.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:17:1.hebrew: שמא תאבד לו מחט - קודם לכן, ואתי השתא לעיוני בתרה. וכיון דמתכוין אף למחט, לאו שליח מצוה הוא, וניזוק:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:17:1.english: Lest a needle be lost to him - [It was lost] beforehand, and he now comes to search for it. And since he also intends [to search] for the needle, he is not an emissary of a mitzvah, and [may be] harmed.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:18:1.hebrew: וכה"ג - דמתכוין למצוה ולצרכו, לאו שליח מצוה הוא?! בתמיה:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:18:1.english: And in a case like this - Where one intends for the mitzvah and for his [own] need, is he not an emissary of a mitzvah?! [This is said] in astonishment.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:1:1.english: Because the light of a lamp is effective for searching - Later on, [the Gemara] explains what its advantage over a torch is.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:2:1.hebrew: לאורה נבדקת - לאור שלה נבדקת, ואין צריך להביא לה אור הנר בלילה, אלא בודקה ביום:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:2:1.english: Is searched by its light - It is searched by its own light, and there is no need to bring the light of a lamp to it at night, but rather one searches it by day.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:3:1.english: And where [is it] - In which place in the room does the light of the skylight not suffice for it [the search]?

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:3:2.hebrew: אי נימא להדי ארובה - נגד החור ממש, אמאי לא? היינו אכסדרה:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:3:2.english: If we say opposite the skylight - Directly opposite the opening — why shouldn't [its light suffice]? That is [the same as] a portico.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:3:3.english: To the sides - Of the opening.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:4:1.hebrew: ונוגה - של עתיד לצדיקים, כאור של שבעת ימי בראשית יהיה:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:4:1.english: And brightness - [The brightness] of the future for the righteous will be like the light of the seven days of Creation.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:4:2.hebrew: קרנים - מלשון כי קרן עור פניו (שמות לד), וזהרורין מיד הקב"ה לו, לצדיק. מזיו של הקב"ה ילכו זהרורין להקרין פני הצדיקים, ולא יהיה אורם שוה לאורו, אלא כנר בפני האבוקה:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:4:2.english: Rays - [This is] in the sense of “that the skin of his face shone” (Exodus 34), and [means that] rays [emanate] from the hand of the Holy One, Blessed be He, to him — to the righteous person. From the radiance of the Holy One, Blessed be He, rays will go forth to make the faces of the righteous shine, and their light will not be equal to His light, but rather like a lamp before a torch.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:5:1.hebrew: אורו לאחריו - ואדם האוחזו, לפניו הוא בודק. הלכך, אין יפה לבדיקה:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:5:1.english: Its light [is] behind it - And a person holding it searches in front of himself. Therefore, it is not good for searching.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:5:2.hebrew: בעית - מתיירא שלא יבעיר את הבית, ואין לבו על הבדיקה יפה:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:5:2.english: Afraid - He is afraid that he might set fire to the house, and his mind is not properly on the search.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:5:3.hebrew: האי משיך נהוריה - אור הנר נמשך ומאריך במקומו, ואינו דולק בקפיצות, אלא נח במקום אחד:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:5:3.english: This [lamp] draws its light - The light of the lamp is continuous and extends in its place, and does not burn in jumps, but rests in one place.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:5:4.hebrew: מיקטף איקטופי - נפסק וקופץ תמיד, לשון הקוטפים מלוח (איוב ל):
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:5:4.english: Fluctuates - [Its light] is constantly severed and leaps, an expression [similar to] "who pluck mallow" (Job 30).

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:6:1.english: "Any" — what does it come to include? - For [the Mishnah] did not teach: "A place into which one brings [leaven]..." etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:6:10.hebrew: החולקת - מעמידין אותה במקום מחיצה לחלק תשמישי הבית, ואורחא דמילתא נקט:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:6:10.english: That divides - They set it up in place of a partition to divide the uses of the house, and [the Tanna] stated the common manner of things.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:6:11.hebrew: ומפסקת - יש הפסק בין שוליה לקרקע, כגון שרגליה גבוהים למטה:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:6:11.english: And [space] separates - There is a space between its underside and the ground, such as where its legs are tall below.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:6:2.english: Holes - That are in the wall.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:6:3.hebrew: העליונים והתחתונים - הגבוהים יותר מדאי והנמוכים יותר מדאי, ואין נוחין להשתמש — אין צריך לבדוק:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:6:3.english: The upper and lower [holes] - Those that are excessively high and those that are excessively low, and are not convenient to use — one does not need to search [them].

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:6:4.hebrew: וגג היציע - אע"פ שהוא נמוך, הואיל ומשופע, אין צריך לבדוק. אבל שאר גגין שלהן לא היו משופעין:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:6:4.english: And the roof of the lean-to - Even though it is low, since it is sloped, it does not require searching. But the rest of their roofs were not sloped.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:6:5.english: A veranda - *Apendiz* [Old French for a wing of a building].

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:6:6.hebrew: גג המגדל - משטיי"ר של עץ, שנותנים לתוכו כלים ואוכלים. תוכו צריך בדיקה, ולא גגו:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:6:6.english: The roof of the closet - A wooden *mestier* [cupboard], into which one puts utensils and food. Its interior requires a search, but not its roof.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:6:7.hebrew: ורפת בקר - שאם היה שם חמץ, הבהמות אכלוהו:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:6:7.english: And a cowshed - For if there was leaven there, the animals ate it.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:6:8.english: And coops - A dwelling place of chickens.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:6:9.hebrew: ומתבן - בית התבן, דמה דרכו של חמץ שם? וכן אוצרות יין ושמן:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:6:9.english: And a storehouse for straw - A shed for straw, for what is the manner of leaven [to be] there? And so too [with] wine cellars and oil storerooms.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:7:1.english: To the point that his hand reaches - For example, where the wall is very thick.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:7:2.english: And [it] separates - There is airspace between its underside and the wood.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:8:1.english: [There is] a contradiction [between the ruling on] holes and [the ruling on] holes - For it taught here that holes require a search.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:9:1.hebrew: הא - דקתני לעיל אין צריכין — בעילאי ותתאי, שאין נוחה תשמישתן, כדקתני בהדיא. והא — באמצעי, שנוחים להשתמש:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:9:1.english: This - That which was taught above, "they do not require [searching]," [refers to] upper and lower [holes], whose use is not convenient, as it taught explicitly. And that [which requires searching refers to] middle [holes], which are convenient to use.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:9:2.hebrew: דמדליא - שגבוהה הרבה, ויש אויר תחתיה הרבה, נוחה תשמישתה:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:9:2.english: That is raised - That it is very high, and there is much space beneath it, [so] its use is convenient.

Rashi on Pesachim 8a:9:3.hebrew: דמיתתאי - אף על פי שיש קצת אויר, אין נוחה תשמישתה:
Rashi on Pesachim 8a:9:3.english: That is low - Even though there is a little space [beneath it], its use is not convenient.

Tosafot on Pesachim 8a:16:1.hebrew: הכא כשהכלב יכול לחפש אחריו - ולכך אינו פטור אלא מפני הסכנה. והא דמשמע גבי מפולת, דאם הכלב יכול לחפש אינו כמבוער וצריך לבערו, ולא מיפטר מפני סכנת עקרב — אור"י: שאני התם, דודאי איכא חמץ — הטריחוהו חכמים להשכיר פועלים במרא וחצינא; אבל הכא, שאין החמץ ידוע — לא הטריחוהו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 8a:16:1.english: "Here, where a dog can search for it" - And therefore, he is exempt [from searching] only because of the danger. And as for that which is implied regarding a rockslide, that if a dog can search for it, it is not considered removed and one must destroy it, and [yet] he is not exempt because of the danger of a scorpion — the Ri says: There it is different, because chametz is definitely there — [so] the Sages troubled him to hire laborers with a hoe and a pickaxe; but here, where the chametz is not known [for certain] — they did not trouble him.

Tosafot on Pesachim 8a:6:1.hebrew: מטה החולקת בתוך הבית ומפסקת - פרש"י דלענין תחתיה מיירי. וקשה: דלפי' לא ה"ל למימר "החולקת", אלא "מפסקת" ותו לא! אלא י"ל: "חולקת בתוך הבית ומפסקת" — היינו שמונחת באמצע הבית; "וחולקת" — היינו שמגעת מכותל לכותל, ואינו יכול לעבור מצד אחר אלא על גבי המטה, או ישוח ויעבור תחתיה; וקאמר דאין צריך בדיקה לצד הפנימי. וכן משמע בירושל' ובתוספתא, דקאמר: רשב"ג אומר, מטה שהיא חוצצת, החולקת בתוך הבית, ועצים ואבנים מונחים תחתיה — בודק צד החיצון ואינו בודק צד הפנימי. ומתוך הירושלמי משמע דברייתא דקתני בה עצים ואבנים גרס: "אין צריך בדיקה". והא דלא משני הכא שיש עצים ואבנים — משום דלא משמע ליה שבשביל כך אין צריך בדיקה, [אלא] משום דאין דרך לשוח ולעבור תחת המטה. ומשני: "הא דמידליא" — התם צריך בדיקה, לפי שרגליה גבוהין ויכול לעבור תחתיה בלא שחייה; אי נמי: במידליא א"צ, דלא ניחא לעלות על גבה ולעבור. וי"ס דגרסי "אין צריך" בקמייתא, ובבתרייתא "צריך"; ולפי גירסא זו, נקט "עצים ואבנים סדורים תחתיה" לרבותא. ור"ח גרס בתרוייהו "אין צריך", ופריך מהא דבקמייתא לא בעינן עצים סדורים, ובבתרייתא בעינן:
Tosafot on Pesachim 8a:6:1.english: "A bed that divides inside the house and separates" - Rashi explained that [the baraita] is dealing with [the space] beneath it. And this is difficult: for according to his explanation, it should not have said "that divides," but rather [only] "and separates," and nothing more! Rather, it can be said: "divides inside the house and separates" means that it is placed in the middle of the house; and "divides" means that it reaches from wall to wall, and one cannot pass to the other side except over the bed, or [by] crouching and passing beneath it; and it states that the inner side does not require a search. And this is also indicated in the Yerushalmi and in the Tosefta, which states: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: [With regard to] a bed that partitions, which divides inside the house, and wood and stones are placed beneath it — one searches the outer side and does not search the inner side. And from the Yerushalmi it is indicated that the baraita that taught "wood and stones" reads "does not require a search." And as for the fact that [the Gemara] here does not resolve [the contradiction by answering] that there are wood and stones — [that is] because it did not seem [plausible] to [the Gemara] that on account of this [alone] it does not require a search, [rather] because it is not typical to crouch and pass beneath the bed. And [the Gemara] resolves: "This [refers to a bed] that is raised" — there it requires a search, because its legs are high and one can pass beneath it without crouching. Alternatively: in [the case of a bed] that is raised, it does not require [a search], because it is not convenient to climb over it and pass [to the inner side]. And there are books that read "does not require [a search]" in the first [baraita], and in the second [baraita] "requires [a search]"; and according to this version, [the second baraita] mentions "wood and stones arranged beneath it" as a novelty. And Rabbeinu Chananel read in both of them "does not require [a search]," and [the Gemara] challenged from the fact that in the first [baraita] we do not require arranged wood, whereas in the second [baraita] we do require [arranged wood].
